messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: streaming p99 latency breach for route 'chat-stream' in us-west-3. p99 > 3.5s sustained for 4m. Autoscaler reports node gpu-west-3-45 with repeated hardware errors (ECC/thermal). Paging on-call.

sanjay: ack — I'm on it. grabbing graphs and checking recent deploys.

megan: seeing elevated correctable ECC counts on that node in the last 30m. also multiple thermal throttle events. node label: gpu-west-3-45 (rack r3b, provider: colo-az3).

kai: quick question — any recent model changes or traffic spikes? I don't see a deployment around the window. traffic +11% but nothing huge.

sanjay: Grafana quick metrics: chat-stream p95 from 0.42s -> 0.58s; p99 jumped to 3.8s. streaming stall rate (connection stall) up x6. KPIs: active streams 1.2k, queued requests backlog 400.

megan: running diagnostics on the host now. pulling `nvidia-smi` and kernel logs. will paste output.

megan: ```
> nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,THERMAL
GPU 0000:3B:00.0
    ECC Errors
        Volatile
            Single Bit : 1245
            Double Bit : 0
    Temperature
        GPU Current Temp : 92 C
    Throttle Reasons
        Thermal : Active
        HWSlowdown : Active
```

megan: and dmesg excerpt:
```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (65): PID 1783 Xid 31, GPU has fallen off the bus
[ 1240.123456] kernel: Corrected ECC error, count=1245, func=0x3
[ 1245.654321] nvidia: thermal emergency: GPU 0 throttled
```

kai: that looks like a hardware-level issue. repeated correctable ECC + thermal clamp will still impact throughput (stalling on kernel retries).

sanjay: mitigation plan: 1) quickly remove node from routing (prevent new streams), 2) drain existing sessions gracefully, 3) route new traffic to warm fallback pool (gpu-west-1 + dedicated reserved), 4) spin up a small-capacity CPU fallback for low-latency control plane ops if needed.

megan: commands I'm about to run: `rnyctl nodes mark-unhealthy gpu-west-3-45 --reason "ecc+thermal"` then `rnyctl drain gpu-west-3-45 --grace=30s --include-streams=true`. Also set placement weight to 0 for that AZ.

kai: I'll update routing policy: set chat-stream route fallback to gpu-west-1 with immediate preference and enable instant fanout to dedicated pool. patch: `/api/v1/routing/policy PATCH {"route":"chat-stream","priority":"failover","targets":["gpu-west-1","dedicated-usw"]}` (I'll apply now).

sanjay: starting drain. will monitor streaming retry rates and token costs. tagging incident as P1 and creating incident page. support-bot: please notify top-tier customers in the next 10m with ETA.

support-bot: Notifying customers with affected SLAs: message queued to CS. Template: "We detected degraded streaming latency; we've routed traffic to fallback infrastructure and are working on resolving root cause. We'll follow up in 30 minutes"

marco: infra note — opening hardware ticket with colo ops. collecting `sosreport`, `dmesg`, `nvidia-smi -q`, and prometheus snapshots. Will request replacement GPU if ECC continues to grow after evacuation.

megan: drain finished, node cordoned: `rnyctl node cordon gpu-west-3-45` -> success. active streams on that node gracefully drained in ~38s. routing now shifted.

sanjay: immediate metrics after failover: p95 -> 0.44s, p99 -> 0.92s (first 2m). streaming stall rate down to baseline. good.

kai: pushing a temporary config to reduce per-connection KV-cache pressure: reduce prefetch size for chat-stream to 64 tokens. This reduces memory footprint on fallback GPUs.

megan: saved diagnostic bundle to incident ticket: https://redwood.internal/incidents/6601112222/artifacts (contains nvidia-smi, dmesg, sosreport).

marco: HW ticket 2026-COLO-789 opened with provider, requester: infra@redwood.com. they've acked and scheduled a physical check in 4 hours. asked to swap card if ECC error rate doesn't fall.

sanjay: impact summary for postmortem: - Duration: spike started ~6601112210, routing mitigation at 6601112245. - Customer impact: ~4 customers saw >5s stalls, approx 0.03% of requests affected. - Root cause (suspected): GPU experiencing repeated correctable ECC events and thermal throttling causing kernel-level stalls.

megan: additional note — we saw a correlated slight rise in KV cache misses on that node prior to ECC spike; hypothesizing thermal-induced HW retries that slowed memory ops. adding to RCA checklist.

kai: follow-ups: 1) mark node quarantined in inventory, 2) add regression alert for per-node ECC velocity (dECC/dt), 3) run predictive replacement job for similar aged nodes. I'll file infra tasks.

marco: will coordinate maintenance and replacement. will confirm when hardware swap complete.

sanjay: for now we keep incident open for post-mortem and until colo confirms hardware status. monitoring window 60m. I've added action items in the incident doc and assigned owners.

support-bot: CS update sent. internal status page updated: "mitigation in place, routing fallback applied; monitoring."

incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Mitigation applied and verified. p99 back under SLO for the route. Incident remains open for follow-up and RCA.

sanjay: thanks team. I'll run through the RCA template and schedule a 1hr postmortem sync tomorrow.

megan: dropping one more logfile snippet into the ticket for HW: `smartctl -a /dev/nvme0n1` and `ipmitool sdr list`.

marco: will update when colo confirms swap.

sanjay: ending active paging — monitoring only. ping if regressions.

incident-bot: Incident 6601112222: paging suspended, status=mitigated, monitoring window=60m.
